what: a modelled M10 thread on a d10 shaft whose root at the d16 shoulder has an r1 fillet: it stops clear of the fillet
method: the fillet's ring: the corner square [5,6]x[10,11] less the quarter disc about (6,11), V_f = 2 pi (5.5 - pi/4 (6 - 4/(3 pi))), its centroid z from the same moments; the cylinder face starts at z=11, where the fillet meets it. the shaft's lower end (z=11) is a shoulder (the fillet and the collar lies past it, in the groove's way), so the groove stops there with its widest part clear of it: its centre w = (P/4 + 2 (d/2 + 0.05P - r_root) tan30)/2 = 0.699551 mm above the shoulder (its half width at the tool's outer edge, 0.05 P past the crest), and the square stop inside material removes exactly as if the groove ended at its centre (see 003); the top end is free, the groove runs out into the air. V = pi 8^2 10 + V_f + pi 5^2 (1 + w) + 2 pi int_{11+w}^35 int r m(r) dr dz. Tolerance 0.05%: SMLib's exact screw sweep
